- Overestimate prices in the short term after positive sentiment spikes; model tends to overshoot early in the 30-day horizon.
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is negative or neutral, especially in the first 7–10 days of the forecast window.
- Model exhibits mean reversion bias: overreacts to recent price spikes, then forecasts a sharp drop that doesn’t fully materialize.
- When sentiment turns negative mid-horizon, model fails to adjust downward quickly — often underestimates the depth of the correction.
- Forecast accuracy degrades as horizon extends beyond 15 days; model overconfidently assumes trend continuation.
- Strong positive sentiment early in the 18-day history correlates with overestimation in the first 5–7 days of the 30d forecast.
- Negative sentiment in the last 3–5 days of history often leads to underestimation in the final 5–7 days of forecast — model ignores tail risk.
- Model tends to ignore sentiment volatility — if sentiment swings sharply, forecast doesn’t adjust for volatility clustering.
